newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, upward pressure on call.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, upward pressure on call.

text.p: Dutch money rates were stable on Tuesday and dealers noted only slight upward pressure on call money rates as the government needed extra liquidity, dealers said.
"Some tax payments were somewhat delayed and the government was therefore seeking extra liquidity," said one dealer, adding the upward pressure on call money rates was already diminishing.
Call money rates were bid between 3.06 and 3.12 percent versus 3.06 percent on Monday and 3.00 percent during some previous sessions.
Dealers said the market was awaiting today's outcome of the U.S. FOMC meeting and some said an increase of U.S. interest rates by 25 basis points was widely expected.
The guilder gained strength, trading at 112.4175 per 100 marks after recently lingering around 112.60 per 100 marks.
"If the guilder moves close to 112.00 per 100 marks we might expect a trimming of the special advances," said one dealer, adding it was much too early for such a move.
The Dutch central bank will set a new special advances pact on Wednesday.
The special advances pact was raised to 2.90 percent on March 10 from 2.70 percent in response to guilder weakness.
Dealers said most business was done in the shorter-end with the focus on call money and one-week deposits.
